argument:
Gamuda's 19% construction-profit growth and improved CFO are substantive, but group profit grew only 5% at 29.35x trailing earnings. Property profit fell 18%, gearing rose from 53% to 72%, and short-term borrowing increased to RM6.341bn from RM2.906bn. Those measured changes raise funding and rollover sensitivity despite a profitable backlog.

RM807.6m CFO did not match RM3.401bn investing outflow; RM3.389bn financing inflow supports the bull's admission that expansion is not self-funding. The RM61.2bn order book can generate value only with funded collections and execution. Management's late-FY27 gearing target is a prospective repair plan. The constructive trend does not offset current financing dependence or establish returns high enough to justify the growth-priced valuation.
key_points: Gearing and short-term borrowing increased substantially.
Valuation anticipates stronger group conversion than observed.
rebuttal_to_previous: Construction profit growth is the bull's strongest evidence, but collections have not funded the broader investment program: RM807.6m CFO versus RM3.401bn investing outflow. A future gearing target does not repair that observed dependence.
